title: Document understanding: OCR vs layout vs vision LLM
summary: Four ways to read a document: layout or OCR only, a Document Intelligence form model, a Content Understanding analyzer, or a vision LLM called directly. They differ in fields, confidence, grounding, cost and where they can run.
useIf: You turn scans, forms, contracts or reports into text or typed fields and must pick the tool by document shape, evidence need and hosting.
avoidIf: The document is already clean digital text with no layout that matters. Plain text extraction is enough.

explain.md: Microsoft's tool guide separates the choices [[r10]] (checked 2026-10-13). For **OCR or layout only**, use Content Understanding `prebuilt-read` or `prebuilt-layout`, which cost less and return richer layout. For **standard forms** (invoice, receipt, ID, tax, mortgage), use a Document Intelligence prebuilt model. For **contracts and unstructured text**, use `prebuilt-contract` or a zero-shot custom analyzer. For labelled custom extraction on structured forms, use a Document Intelligence custom model, which can start from as few as 5 labelled samples. **On-premises or air-gapped**, Document Intelligence containers are the only option. Build directly on a vision model only when you need full model and prompt control.

A direct vision LLM call is flexible but you then build chunking, confidence and grounding yourself. Versions: Content Understanding GA is `2025-11-01`, while `2026-06-01-preview` adds agentic mode, in-page segmentation, signature detection and document metadata. Document Intelligence v4.0 is GA as `2024-11-30` and needs no migration. In Azure AI Search the Document Layout skill stays supported, but new skillsets should use the Content Understanding skill [[r12]].

pitfalls.fix: Use the Content Understanding skill in AI Search, which handles cross-page tables, or merge tables after extraction.

scenarios.title: Contracts with implied dates
scenarios.situation: A legal team extracts renewal terms, notice periods and parties from thousands of supplier contracts. Layouts vary and some terms are implied by clauses.
scenarios.question: Which reader?

options.name: Content Understanding `prebuilt-contract` or a zero-shot analyzer, on GA `2025-11-01`
options.why: The tool guide points contracts and unstructured text to these [[r10]].
options.tradeoff: Cloud only, and you must test field accuracy.

options.name: Document Intelligence custom model
options.why: Works if layouts are consistent and you can label samples.
options.tradeoff: Brittle when layouts change and fields are inferred.

options.name: Layout service alone
options.why: Returns text and structure but no typed fields.
options.tradeoff: Right when the goal is only to index contract text.

flips.if: Contracts must be processed on premises
flips.then: Document Intelligence containers with a custom model.
A direct vision call with human review may be enough.

scenarios.takeaway: Unstructured and inferred fields suit an analyzer.

scenarios.title: Stable inspection forms in a plant
scenarios.situation: A plant with no internet scans its own inspection form, a fixed layout that is not a standard type. Hundreds of labelled examples exist.
scenarios.question: What do you deploy?

options.name: Document Intelligence custom model in a container
options.why: Containers are the only on-premises option, and custom models can start from as few as 5 labelled samples [[r10]].
options.tradeoff: You run and update containers and keep labelling.

options.name: Content Understanding analyzer
options.why: It is a cloud service and cannot run air-gapped.
options.tradeoff: Right for unstructured documents when the cloud is allowed.

options.name: Vision LLM called directly
options.why: Flexible if you can host a model locally.
options.tradeoff: No native confidence or grounding, so you build validation yourself.

flips.if: The plant gets a secured cloud link
flips.then: Re-evaluate the managed analyzer for new document types.

flips.if: The form is a standard invoice

scenarios.takeaway: A no-cloud rule decides the tool before accuracy does.

quiz.q: A stable internal form must be read in an air-gapped plant with field confidence. Which tool fits?
options: Vision LLM through a cloud API
A layout service in the cloud
quiz.explain: Document Intelligence containers are the only on-premises option among these. The others are cloud services or need a cloud call.

flashcards.front: Which tool is the only on-premises option for document reading in Microsoft's guide?
flashcards.back: Document Intelligence containers. Content Understanding and direct cloud vision calls need the cloud.

flashcards.front: How many labelled samples can a Document Intelligence custom model start from?
flashcards.back: As few as 5 labelled samples (neural model), per Microsoft's tool-choice guide.

flashcards.front: Which Content Understanding API version is for production?
flashcards.back: GA `2025-11-01`. `2026-06-01-preview` has no SLA. Document Intelligence v4.0 GA is `2024-11-30` and needs no migration.
